definitions.verifier_doc: Minimal template verifier that always scores 1.0. Intended as a starting point for new eval implementations; not for production use.

eval_config_fields.label: Ungradeable Causes Scored As Zero
eval_config_fields.description: Causes this world will accept as a scored 0.0 rather than a voided grading run. Empty by default, which keeps every cause fatal. It matters because an errored verifier is not local: most scoring methods refuse to score a run that contains one, so a judge that reached no verdict on a single criterion discards every other verifier's grade in the same rubric. List a cause here when failing that one criterion is the more honest outcome than losing the whole grade. Infrastructure causes (snapshot_unreadable, disk_exhausted, config_error, model_unavailable) are usually best left fatal, since the grade really is void.

eval_config_fields.label: Harness
eval_config_fields.description: Which agent drives the judge. claude_code speaks the Anthropic API and antigravity speaks Gemini, so the grading model has to match the one chosen. opencode reaches models through the proxy and drives any of them, but cannot enforce max_iterations, leaving wall_clock_seconds as the only bound. Every grade records the harness that produced it, so runs on different harnesses stay separable.

eval_config_fields.label: Grading Model
eval_config_fields.description: Model override for this world. Declared at eval-config level on purpose so a world can pin the model but an individual task cannot, otherwise a pooled analysis mixes two graders with no way to separate them. Must be a model the selected Harness can drive: Claude Code grades on Anthropic Claude models, Antigravity on Gemini, and opencode on anything the proxy routes. Anything else is refused before the spawn. Left empty, the run's own judge grades when the harness can drive it, and that harness's own model grades when it cannot.

eval_config_fields.label: Grading Policy Override
eval_config_fields.description: Optional replacement for the verifier's static built-in policy body only. Leave empty to use the built-in policy. The runner still adds runtime workspace notes for the reference artifact and prompt files, plus its prompt-injection defense, because those facts and safety rules are runner-owned. The policy body defines the criteria-ledger contract: `guidance` versus `beyond_guidance` tagging, beyond-guidance findings being score-neutral, and when `ungradeable` applies. An override that does not restate those rules leaves those output fields to a model that was never told what they mean.

eval_config_fields.label: Scratch Workspace
eval_config_fields.description: When enabled, the judge can write UTF-8 notes under scratch/ with its write_scratch_file tool. Those files persist during the grading session and are saved for human inspection; they are judge-authored scratchwork, not evidence from the graded agent.

eval_config_fields.label: Max Iterations
eval_config_fields.description: Tool-loop step limit before the run is marked ungradeable. 200 is both the default and the maximum, so set this only to spend less. Observed runs of one task took 55, 32 and 19 steps, so a budget in the tens will fail some of them.

eval_config_fields.label: Wall Clock Seconds
eval_config_fields.description: Per-run wall-clock budget in seconds before the run is cut off. Defaults to 3600 and cannot exceed 7200. An observed run took 12 minutes 39 seconds, so a budget near 900 leaves little headroom.

verifier_config_fields.label: Grader Guidance
verifier_config_fields.description:
Expert-authored instructions for the judge. Cover the context, the reference artifact, the must-haves, the common failures and the acceptable variation. Severity belongs in the wording rather than in numbers or weights.

IMPORTANT: supply a golden snapshot whenever one exists. Goldens land under reference/ in the judge's workspace and their files are listed in the prompt. Measured on real deliverables: an unanchored run scored a failing brief 1.00 three times out of three, while the same verifier with a reference correctly scored a failing run 0.28. Unanchored graders inflate.

verifier_config_fields.label: Structured Criterion Definitions
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional complete criterion list for critical-count reporting. Each entry requires a unique criterion_id, criterion text, and a boolean critical flag. The judge returns those IDs; criticality comes from this authored metadata. Unset or empty keeps the existing free-form grading contract.

verifier_output_fields.label: Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Judge's score, 0.0 to 1.0.

verifier_output_fields.label: Summary
verifier_output_fields.description: One or two reviewer-facing sentences about overall quality and the most consequential gaps.

verifier_output_fields.label: Detailed Reasoning
verifier_output_fields.description: Full audit detail and evidence supporting the score.

verifier_output_fields.label: Ungradeable
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the verifier reached no judgement. Two shapes, and Score tells them apart. Normally the row is an ERROR and carries no Score at all, so it cannot enter an average. When the world lists the cause in Ungradeable Causes Scored As Zero the row is OK and its 0.0 is a real grade for a criterion the judge could not establish. Filter on this flag to separate either kind from a zero the judge actually awarded.

verifier_output_fields.label: Ungradeable Reason
verifier_output_fields.description: Human-readable detail for an ungradeable row, including the underlying error where there was one. Read this when Ungradeable is true to see why the run produced no grade.

verifier_output_fields.label: No Deliverable
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the agent produced no files at all. This is a real 0.0 and not an error: nothing was delivered, so nothing met the guidance. Keep these in score averages, and read the flag when you want to separate 'did nothing' from 'did it badly'.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Ledger
verifier_output_fields.description: One entry per requirement assessed: the criterion, met or not met, the evidence, and whether it came from the Grader Guidance or was judged beyond it.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criterion Definitions Used for This Grade
verifier_output_fields.description: Authored criterion IDs, text and criticality retained with this result. Absent for legacy free-form grading.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Assessed
verifier_output_fields.description: How many requirements the verifier ruled on.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Met
verifier_output_fields.description: How many assessed requirements passed.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Not Met
verifier_output_fields.description: How many SCORED requirements failed, meaning those drawn from the Grader Guidance. Findings beyond the guidance are counted separately and do not move the score.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Beyond Guidance
verifier_output_fields.description: How many requirements the verifier judged that the guidance did not name. A high number means the guidance is thin.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Beyond Guidance Not Met
verifier_output_fields.description: Unrequested requirements the verifier judged and found wanting. These do not affect the score; they are the candidates to fold into the next revision of the guidance.

verifier_output_fields.label: Grading Model (resolved)
verifier_output_fields.description: The model that actually produced this score. Recorded so a pooled analysis can separate graders.

verifier_output_fields.label: Model Was Substituted
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the grading run's own judge could not drive the harness, so the harness's fallback model graded instead. A score with this set was not produced by the model the run was configured with.

verifier_output_fields.label: Harness (resolved)
verifier_output_fields.description: The agent harness that drove this grading run. The same model on two harnesses gets different tools and a different loop, so pooling them compares two graders.

verifier_output_fields.label: Harness Version
verifier_output_fields.description: The harness build that ran, read at grading time and empty when it could not be determined. A harness upgrade moves scores, so a comparison needs it recorded per run.

verifier_output_fields.label: Grader Guidance (as run for this grade)
verifier_output_fields.description: The guidance this run graded against. Distinct from the verifier's `grader_guidance`, which is the text as it stands now: editing overwrites that copy in place, so without this a past grade can only be shown beside instructions it may never have read.

verifier_output_fields.label: Grading Policy Override (as run for this grade)
verifier_output_fields.description: The grading policy override this run read, or an empty string when the built-in policy was used. Eval-config values are overwritten in place when edited, so this preserves the judge input that produced a past grade without copying the built-in prompt onto every grade.

verifier_output_fields.label: Score (0-100)
verifier_output_fields.description: The same judgement on a 0 to 100 scale.

verifier_output_fields.label: Had Reference
verifier_output_fields.description: True when a reference artifact was available to compare against.

verifier_output_fields.label: Tool Calls
verifier_output_fields.description: Number of inspection steps the judge took.

verifier_output_fields.label: Extraction Skipped Files
verifier_output_fields.description: Files the size caps dropped from the judge's workspace. When nonzero the judge graded a partial view of the deliverable.

verifier_output_fields.label: Flattened Database Tables
verifier_output_fields.description: Snapshot tables with columns loaded as text because their original definitions could not be recreated. SQL comparisons on these tables may be misleading.

verifier_output_fields.label: Verdict Salvaged
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the judge's verdict did not parse and only the score could be recovered, which an output limit is the usual cause of. The score is the judge's own, but the criteria counts on this row are zero because the salvage recovers no criteria, not because the judge found nothing. Exclude these rows from any criteria analysis. They are valid for score analysis.

verifier_output_fields.label: Truncated App State Files
verifier_output_fields.description: Files the size ceiling cost the .apps_data/ tree. Usually seed state, so the run is still scored, but a task that delivers through an app has its graded artifact in there and a nonzero value means the judge saw part of it.

verifier_output_fields.label: Ungradeable Cause
verifier_output_fields.description: Why the run produced no judgement, as a stable code rather than the English in Reason: config_error, model_unavailable, snapshot_unreadable, disk_exhausted, deliverable_truncated, all_files_over_caps, no_verdict, judge_declined. Absent on rows that carry a real score.

verifier_output_fields.label: Truncated Deliverable Files
verifier_output_fields.description: Files the size budget cost the agent's own output. Nonzero means the judge never saw part of the work, so the run is ungradeable rather than a scored zero.

verifier_output_fields.label: Prompt Files Seen
verifier_output_fields.description: Files the task's prompt attached, as carried on the trajectory. Zero on a task known to attach one means the attachment never reached grading.

verifier_output_fields.label: Prompt Files Written
verifier_output_fields.description: Prompt attachments the judge could open under source='prompt_files'. Fewer than seen means the size caps or a malformed payload stopped the rest.

verifier_output_fields.label: Prompt Files Skipped
verifier_output_fields.description: Attachments the size caps or a malformed payload kept out of the workspace. Nonzero means the judge could not open something the task meant it to see.

verifier_output_fields.label: Prompt Files By Reference
verifier_output_fields.description: Attachments carried as a path rather than inline data, so nothing was staged for them. Counted so Seen reconciles as Written plus Skipped plus By Reference.

verifier_output_fields.label: Prompt Files Bytes
verifier_output_fields.description: Attachment bytes staged for the judge. Prompt attachments are the one tree bounded by a fixed cap rather than by the snapshot's own manifest, so this is how close that cap is to binding.

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge Scratchwork
verifier_output_fields.description: Judge-authored scratchwork captured from scratch/ for human inspection. Each entry includes its relative path, byte size and content. These files are not evidence from the graded agent and must not be mistaken for deliverables, references or proof of task completion.

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge Scratchwork File Count
verifier_output_fields.description: Number of judge-authored scratchwork files captured.

verifier_output_fields.label: Session Cost (USD)
verifier_output_fields.description: What this grading session cost, as the harness's own SDK reported it. On the row because the budget meter cannot see it: the harness reaches the provider from a subprocess rather than through the metered call path. 0 when the harness reports usage but not spend — read alongside 'Session Usage Reported'. A Studio-local operational figure, not the canonical cost: CAS carries token counts and the warehouse prices them from Studio's rate card, so a finance-facing number belongs there rather than in a sum over this column.

verifier_output_fields.label: Session Cache Read Tokens
verifier_output_fields.description: Prompt tokens this session read from cache. Worlds that run several agentic verifiers per grading run open every session with the same preamble, so zero across all of them means each paid full input rate for identical text.

verifier_output_fields.label: Session Input Tokens
verifier_output_fields.description: Prompt tokens this session sent. Read alongside the cache reads: the ratio is what says whether caching is working.

verifier_output_fields.label: Session Attempted
verifier_output_fields.description: Whether a grading session was actually started. False means the run ended first (no guidance, unreadable snapshot), so the zeros above are real. True with 'Session Usage Reported' false means a session ran and reported nothing — including a harness that crashed part-way, whose spend cannot be recovered.

verifier_output_fields.label: Session Usage Reported
verifier_output_fields.description: Whether the harness reported any cost or token figure for this session. False means the numbers above are absent, not zero — filter on this before summing or before reading a zero cache-read as evidence that caching is not working.

definitions.verifier_doc: Grades a deliverable with an LLM that inspects the files itself, rather than judging one fixed text extraction. The judge can read the same file as text, as rendered images or as native structure, so formatting a text extraction discards stays reachable. It receives expert guidance and an optional reference artifact, and is deliberately not given the task's rubric. Only criteria drawn from the guidance move the score; anything it judges beyond the guidance is reported for the expert and deliberately not priced.

verifier_config_fields.label: Rubric
verifier_config_fields.description: The rule to check against the final turn, written as a statement about the response. Phrase it as the rule itself even when it has been superseded — 'expected behavior' below decides whether following it counts as a pass.

verifier_config_fields.label: Source
verifier_config_fields.description: Which authority tier the rule came from. When rules conflict, the tier decides which one wins.

verifier_config_fields.label: Instruction From Turn
verifier_config_fields.description: The turn that introduced this rule — where it came from, not the turn being graded. Grading always targets the final turn.

verifier_config_fields.label: Expected Behavior
verifier_config_fields.description: SATISFIED: the model should comply. OVERRIDEN: a later instruction replaced this rule, so the model should NOT comply and the score is inverted — following a dead rule is the failure being measured.

verifier_config_fields.label: Overridden By
verifier_config_fields.description: Comma-separated ids of the rubrics that supersede this one. Leave empty unless Expected Behavior is OVERRIDEN.

verifier_config_fields.label: Overridden Reason
verifier_config_fields.description: Why the other rule wins. Required when Overridden By is set. RECENCY covers the common case of a later developer instruction replacing an earlier one.

verifier_config_fields.label: Grading Target
verifier_config_fields.description: Which part of the output to grade. MCDI conversations are graded on the model's final message unless the task writes files.
options: All output (modified files and final message in console)

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge Grade
verifier_output_fields.description: Whether the model behaved correctly on this rubric, after applying Expected Behavior. Not the raw judge verdict.

verifier_output_fields.label: Rationale
verifier_output_fields.description: The judge's reasoning about the criterion.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criterion Literally Met
verifier_output_fields.description: The raw judge verdict before inversion. Kept so an overridden rubric that reads as a pass while the criterion was not met is legible, and so a correct flip can be told apart from a judge that got it wrong.

verifier_output_fields.label: Score Inverted
verifier_output_fields.description: True when Expected Behavior is OVERRIDEN.

verifier_config_fields.label: Indago report path
verifier_config_fields.description: Path to report.json inside the trajectory snapshot's filesystem/ root.

verifier_config_fields.label: Indago markdown report path
verifier_config_fields.description: Used only for the summary-fidelity check. Absent is fine — a run that failed before reporting writes no report.md.

verifier_config_fields.label: Judge model override
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional override for the judge model. If empty, the grading run's default judge is used. A default here would be copied into verifier_values at creation and would then silently outrank the run's choice. Used only to separate 'found' from 'adjacent'; misses and coverage failures are decided without a model.

verifier_output_fields.label: Bucket
verifier_output_fields.description: found | adjacent | missed | not_scanned | error. 'not_scanned' means the prioritiser never opened the target file, which is a coverage failure rather than a detection failure.

verifier_output_fields.label: Total findings reported
verifier_output_fields.description: Volume signal, not a precision score. The golden set knows one vulnerability per case, so a finding elsewhere is not thereby a false positive.

verifier_output_fields.label: Summary fidelity
verifier_output_fields.description: pass | fail | indeterminate | error | not_applicable. `error` means the check itself failed (judge timeout or provider error); `not_applicable` means there was nothing to check. Conflating them lets a pass rate computed over 'applicable' cases silently drop the failures. `indeterminate` means no contradiction was found among the findings the check could see, but some were dropped to fit the prompt -- truncation can hide a contradiction, so that is not a pass. A SEPARATE metric from the detection bucket and never merged into the score: Indago's executive summary is written by a stage that never sees the final findings (SECPRJ-1920), so it can contradict them. The delta between this and detection is the diagnostic.

verifier_output_fields.label: Summary findings omitted
verifier_output_fields.description: Findings dropped from the summary-fidelity prompt. Non-zero is why a check reads `indeterminate` rather than `pass`.

verifier_output_fields.label: Answer-key file(s)
verifier_output_fields.description: The file the fix changed, or every changed file when the fix spans several. Echoed back so a result is readable without the task beside it.

verifier_output_fields.label: Scanned path
verifier_output_fields.description: The scan root Indago recorded, from the report.

verifier_output_fields.label: Scanned coverage
verifier_output_fields.description: focused | balanced | thorough, as the run actually ran. Cases are only comparable at equal coverage.

verifier_output_fields.label: Scanner-only run
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the run stopped at the candidate stage with no validation. Says whether `other_finding_count` may be read as anything more than reviewer burden -- it is never a false-positive rate.

verifier_output_fields.label: Other findings
verifier_output_fields.description: Findings that are not the answer key. Reviewer burden, recorded as context and never as a rate.

verifier_output_fields.label: Findings judged
verifier_output_fields.description: How many findings actually reached the judge.

verifier_output_fields.label: Findings omitted
verifier_output_fields.description: Findings dropped to fit the judge prompt. Normally zero. A `missed` with any omission is reported as an ERROR, not a score, because the answer may be in what was dropped.

verifier_output_fields.label: Locations omitted
verifier_output_fields.description: affectedLocations cut by the per-finding render cap. Locations matching a target file are ordered FIRST, so a non-zero value here is non-target noise unless one finding names more than the cap in targets -- it does not mean the answer was hidden. Recorded because a depressed score and a hidden answer must not look alike.

verifier_output_fields.label: Line accuracy
verifier_output_fields.description: How often a cited line actually contains the symbol cited with it. Instrument check on the ranking signal, never a result about detection: it separates 'the finding is not near the fix' from 'the line numbers were wrong'.

verifier_output_fields.label: Locations checked for line accuracy
verifier_output_fields.description: Denominator for line_accuracy; 0 means unmeasured.

verifier_output_fields.label: Hunk tolerance (lines)
verifier_output_fields.description: Slack allowed when testing a finding's line against a fix hunk. Recorded per case so a corpus can say whether it is set anywhere near right.

verifier_output_fields.label: Findings on a changed line
verifier_output_fields.description: Findings citing a line the fix actually changed, when indago_fix_hunks is supplied. A pre-filter for the judge, not a verdict.

definitions.verifier_doc:
# Indago Golden Match

Scores one Indago security scan against a golden-set answer key: a vulnerability
that really shipped, and the pull request that really fixed it.

## Overview

The task filesystem holds a repository at the commit *before* its fix landed, so
nothing in the code hints at the bug. The scanner writes `outputs/report.json`;
this verifier decides whether the scan found the vulnerability the answer key
describes.

Coverage is settled before detection. A scan that never opened the target file
has not missed the bug -- it was never shown it -- so that case scores
`not_scanned` rather than `missed`. Collapsing the two hides harness failures
inside the detection number (SECPRJ-1908).

## Supported Inputs

An Indago `report.json` in the task's output snapshot, plus the answer-key task
fields written by `scripts/indago/stage_cases.py`. `report.md` is read only as a
fallback when the structured summary is absent.

## Configuration

| Field | Purpose |
| -- | -- |
| `report_path` | Structured report. Defaults to `outputs/report.json`. |
| `summary_path` | Markdown fallback for the summary check. Defaults to `outputs/report.md`. |
| `judge_model` | Optional override. Empty means the grading run's judge. Pinning one judge across a corpus matters, because cases graded by different judges are not comparable. |

## Scoring

`found` 1.0 · `adjacent` 0.5 · `missed` 0.0 · `not_scanned` 0.0.

A configuration or artifact problem returns ERROR rather than a silent zero, and
so does any verdict short of `found` reached without showing the judge every
finding -- the answer may be in what was dropped.

## Limitations

**Recall only.** These runs are scanner-only; the validation stage that prunes
false positives cannot run on library CVEs. `other_finding_count` and
`scanner_only` are recorded as context, never as a rate. Scoring precision here
would measure the product at a stage it is not meant to be judged at.

**Summary fidelity is separate and never folded into the score.** Indago's
executive summary is written by a stage that never sees the final findings
(SECPRJ-1920), so it can assert "no confidentiality findings" while a body below
it names the exact vulnerability. The delta between the two numbers is the
diagnostic; merging them destroys it.

**Line numbers are model-reported and drift** -- measured at 87.5% accuracy on a
real report. Hunk matching carries a tolerance and `line_accuracy` is emitted per
case, so a low overlap rate can be told apart from instrument error.
definitions.limitations: Measures recall only -- no precision metric, by design.

verifier_config_fields.description:
What this verifier checks (e.g., 'Q3 2025 LA net taxable sales = $14,500').

This verifier calculates values from Orders/Refunds CSV data:

BASIC CALCULATIONS:
- Net Taxable Sales = SUM(orders.amount) - SUM(refunds.amount)
- Sales Tax Collected = SUM(orders.sales_tax)
- Net Sales Tax = SUM(orders.sales_tax) - SUM(refunds.sales_tax)

ZIP/CITY FILTERING:
- Net Taxable Sales by ZIP: Filter by "to_zip" column, then calculate net
- Sales Tax by ZIP: Filter by "to_zip", sum sales_tax

RATE CORRECTIONS:
- Corrected Tax with Rate: net_taxable × corrected_rate
- Additional Tax to Remit: corrected_tax - original_net_tax

PROJECTIONS:
- Projected Sales = base_amount × (1 + growth_rate)
- Projected Tax = projected_sales × tax_rate

# Spreadsheet Verifier

Validates cell values and formatting in CSV and Excel files within a trajectory's final snapshot.

## Overview

The Spreadsheet Verifier inspects specific cells in spreadsheet files to confirm that a model's output meets expected criteria. It supports two categories of checks: **value checks** (comparing cell contents) and **formatting checks** (inspecting visual properties like bold, highlight color, or formulas). Use this verifier when the task requires the model to produce or modify a spreadsheet and you need to verify specific cells are correct.

## Supported Inputs

| File Type | Extensions | Value Checks | Formatting Checks |
|-----------|------------|:------------:|:-----------------:|
| CSV       | `.csv`     | Yes          | No                |
| Excel     | `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.xls` | Yes | Yes        |

The verifier reads files from the trajectory's final snapshot archive (ZIP). Formatting checks (highlight, text color, bold, formula) require an Excel file -- configuring them against a CSV will produce an error.

## Configuration

### File Pattern

Glob pattern to locate the file inside the snapshot archive.

| Example | Matches |
|---------|---------|
| `*.xlsx` | Any Excel file |
| `*.csv` | Any CSV file |
| `output.xlsx` | Exact filename |
| `reports/*.csv` | CSV files in a `reports/` subdirectory |

If multiple files match, only the **first** match is checked (order depends on the ZIP archive, which is non-deterministic). Always prefer an exact filename to avoid ambiguity.

### Sheet Name

For Excel files, specifies which sheet to inspect. If omitted, defaults to the **first sheet by index** (i.e., the leftmost tab),Ignored for CSV files.

### Cell Reference

Identifies which cell(s) to check. Supports:

- **Single cell**: `A1`, `B2`, `Z99`
- **Range**: `B2:B10`, `A1:D5`

For ranges, each cell in the range is checked individually against the configured rule. Ranges are **inclusive** on both ends (e.g., `B2:B5` checks B2, B3, B4, and B5). Cell references must stay within the actual data bounds -- out-of-bounds cells will fail with an error, so do not use oversized ranges as a "check entire sheet" workaround.

## Check Types

### Value Checks

These work on both CSV and Excel files.

| Check Type | Description | Required Fields |
|------------|-------------|-----------------|
| `value_exact_match` | Cell value must exactly equal the expected value | `expected_value` |
| `value_contains` | Cell value must contain the expected substring | `expected_value` |
| `value_not_contains` | Cell value must not contain the expected substring | `expected_value` |
| `value_regex` | Cell value must match the regular expression | `expected_value` (regex pattern) |
| `value_equals_number` | Cell numeric value must equal the expected number | `expected_value` (number) |
| `value_greater_than` | Cell numeric value must be greater than minimum | `expected_min` |
| `value_less_than` | Cell numeric value must be less than maximum | `expected_max` |
| `value_between` | Cell numeric value must be within the range | `expected_min`, `expected_max` |
| `value_not_empty` | Cell must have a non-empty value | -- |
| `value_is_empty` | Cell must be empty | -- |

String-based checks (`value_exact_match`, `value_contains`, `value_not_contains`) respect the **Case Sensitive** toggle, which defaults to `false` (case-insensitive).

### Formatting Checks

These require an **Excel** file (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.xls`).

| Check Type | Description | Required Fields |
|------------|-------------|-----------------|
| `formatting_highlight` | Cell fill/background color must match | `expected_highlight` (hex, e.g. `#FFFF00`) |
| `formatting_text_color` | Cell font color must match | `expected_text_color` (hex, e.g. `#FF0000`) |
| `formatting_bold` | Cell font must be bold (or not) | `expected_bold` (true/false) |
| `formatting_formula` | Cell must contain the specified formula | `expected_formula` (e.g. `=SUM(A1:A10)`) |

Colors should be specified as hex strings with a leading `#`. The comparison is case-insensitive.

## Examples

### Verify a specific cell value

- **File Pattern**: `output.xlsx`
- **Cell Reference**: `B2`
- **Check Type**: `value_exact_match`
- **Expected Value**: `42`

Checks that cell B2 in `output.xlsx` contains exactly `42`.

### Verify a range of cells is not empty

- **File Pattern**: `*.xlsx`
- **Cell Reference**: `A1:A10`
- **Check Type**: `value_not_empty`

Each cell from A1 through A10 is checked individually. All must be non-empty for the verifier to pass.

### Verify cell highlighting

- **File Pattern**: `report.xlsx`
- **Cell Reference**: `C5`
- **Check Type**: `formatting_highlight`
- **Expected Highlight Color**: `#FFFF00`

Checks that cell C5 has a yellow background fill.

### Verify a formula exists

- **File Pattern**: `*.xlsx`
- **Cell Reference**: `D10`
- **Check Type**: `formatting_formula`
- **Expected Formula**: `=SUM(D1:D9)`

Checks that D10 contains the exact formula `=SUM(D1:D9)`.

### Numeric range check

- **File Pattern**: `results.csv`
- **Cell Reference**: `B5`
- **Check Type**: `value_between`
- **Minimum Value**: `0`
- **Maximum Value**: `100`

Checks that the numeric value in B5 is between 0 and 100 inclusive.

## Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **Formatting checks on CSV files will error.** CSV files have no formatting metadata. Always use Excel for formatting checks.
- **Multiple file matches use only the first file.** If `*.xlsx` matches 3 files, only the first (by archive order) is checked. Use a specific filename pattern to be explicit.
- **Ranges check each cell individually.** A range like `B2:B10` checks 9 cells. If any one fails, the overall verifier fails.
- **Color matching is case-insensitive.** `#ffff00` and `#FFFF00` are treated as the same color.
- **Empty `expected_value` with `value_exact_match` checks for an empty string**, not a missing cell. Use `value_is_empty` to check for truly empty cells.
- **Numeric checks coerce strings to numbers.** If a cell contains the text `"42"`, `value_equals_number` with expected value `42` will still pass.
- **`value_equals_number` has a 0.01% relative tolerance** (or absolute 0.0001 for zero), so minor rounding differences are handled. Use this instead of `value_exact_match` when comparing numbers where decimal precision may vary.
- **`value_equals_number` strips unit/currency characters before comparing.** Symbols like `$`, `€`, `£`, `¥`, commas, and whitespace are removed. This means `100B` and `100M` would both parse to `100` and incorrectly match. To verify units, use `value_exact_match` or `value_contains` instead.
- **Out-of-bounds cell references fail, not skip.** If a range extends beyond the actual data (e.g., `A1:A100` on a 10-row sheet), every out-of-bounds cell is reported as a failure.
- **Sheet name is ignored for CSV.** Setting a sheet name when checking a CSV file has no effect.

## Scoring

- **Score = 1.0** if every configured check (value and formatting) passes.
- **Score = 0.0** if any single check fails or an error occurs (e.g. file not found, invalid ZIP, formatting check on CSV).

The result summary shows pass/fail counts for each category, e.g. `Values: 3/3 passed | Formatting: 2/2 passed`. On failure, up to 3 failed check reasons are included in the summary with the cell reference.

## Output

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `passed` | boolean | Whether all configured checks passed |
| `reason` | text | Human-readable summary of results |
| `file_checked` | text | Path of the file that was verified inside the snapshot |
| `value_checks` | text | Detailed per-cell results for value checks |
| `formatting_checks` | text | Detailed per-cell results for formatting checks |
| `value_passed_count` | number | Count of value checks that passed |
| `value_total_count` | number | Total number of value checks run |
| `formatting_passed_count` | number | Count of formatting checks that passed |
| `formatting_total_count` | number | Total number of formatting checks run |

# Spreadsheet Verifier (Difficulty Weighted)

A drop-in variant of the [Spreadsheet Verifier](./spreadsheet_verifier.md) with one extra field — **Difficulty** — intended to be paired with the **Difficulty Weighted Average** scoring method.

## When to use this

Use this verifier instead of the plain `spreadsheet_verifier` when:

- A task has multiple spreadsheet checks of varying importance / difficulty, and
- You want easy / hard checks to contribute proportionally more to the final task score, rather than every check counting equally.

If every check on a task should count the same, prefer `spreadsheet_verifier` paired with a simple average scoring method.

## Behavior

The cell-value and formatting-check logic is **identical** to `spreadsheet_verifier`. Each verifier still produces a binary score:

- **Score = 1.0** if every configured check (value and formatting) passes.
- **Score = 0.0** if any single check fails or an error occurs.

See the [Spreadsheet Verifier docs](./spreadsheet_verifier.md) for the full list of supported check types, file types, cell reference formats, and edge cases.

## Difficulty Field

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `difficulty` | `Low` / `Medium` / `High` (default `Medium`) | Expert-assigned difficulty for this check. Drives weighting under the Difficulty Weighted Average scoring method. |

The default Low/Medium/High → weight mapping is **1 / 3 / 5**, but it is overridable per scoring config (`low_weight`, `medium_weight`, `high_weight`).

## Scoring Example

With three checks attached to a task:

| Check | Difficulty | Weight | Result |
|-------|-----------|--------|--------|
| Cell B2 = 42 | Low | 1 | passed (1.0) |
| Range B5:B10 not empty | Medium | 3 | failed (0.0) |
| Formula in D10 = `=SUM(D1:D9)` | High | 5 | passed (1.0) |

Final score = `(1·1 + 3·0 + 5·1) / (1 + 3 + 5)` = `6 / 9` ≈ `0.667`.

## Pairing

Pair with the `difficulty_weighted_average` scoring method. Any verifier that exposes a `difficulty` field on `verifier_values` (e.g. `output_llm_difficulty_weighted`) can be mixed with this one under the same scoring method.

verifier_config_fields.description: The type of verification to perform. 'Existence Check' verifies a specific record exists with expected content. 'Guard (Negative Check)' fails if an unexpected record is found. 'Count Check' verifies the number of matching records. 'Content Match' checks that existing record content matches expectations.

verifier_config_fields.description: The database table to query (e.g., 'Notes', 'invoices'). Must match a table name from the database schema.

verifier_config_fields.description: Where to look for evidence when verifying. 'DB only' checks only the database tables. 'DB with trajectory fallback' checks the DB first, falls back to the run trajectory if the table is empty. 'Trajectory only' checks only the agent's tool calls in the trajectory.

verifier_config_fields.description: Optional free-text notes for anything not covered by the structured fields above. Appended to the structured prompt when generating verifier code. Also kept for reference.

verifier_config_fields.label: Verifier code
verifier_config_fields.description: Python code that defines def check(ctx) -> dict. Return {"passed": bool, "details": str, "score": float?, "metrics": dict?}. Optional "score" (float in [0, 1]) sets the verifier score directly, e.g. for objective metrics like MCC; when omitted the score is 1.0/0.0 from passed. ctx exposes query_db, list_tables, has_table, table_columns, table_row_count for database access, plus read_text, read_json, list_files, exists for filesystem access, and final_answer and trajectory.
verifier_config_fields.default_value:
def check(ctx):
    """Verify the database state after the agent's actions.

    Database access:
      ctx.query_db(sql, params)  - execute SQL, returns list of tuples
      ctx.list_tables()          - all tables, lower-cased
      ctx.has_table(table)       - exists? case-insensitive
      ctx.table_columns(table)   - list column names
      ctx.table_row_count(table) - count rows in a table

    Filesystem access:
      ctx.read_text(path)        - read a snapshot file as text
      ctx.read_json(path)        - parse a snapshot file as JSON
      ctx.list_files(glob)       - list snapshot files matching glob
      ctx.final_answer           - agent's last message (str)

    Return: {"passed": bool, "details": str}
    """
    return {"passed": True, "details": ""}

definitions.verifier_doc:
The baseline-free twin of the Tool-Augmented DB Diff Judge. It judges the FINAL database state instead of a baseline-vs-final diff, so no baseline snapshot is produced, stored or shipped.

Same criteria config and the same output fields as `db_diff_llm` / `db_diff_llm_tools`, so an eval config can be pointed at this eval without touching any of the verifiers underneath it — verifiers reference the eval config, and the eval definition lives on the config. The `.db` scoping carries over too: `.db` entries in a verifier's expected output files choose which database to query, exactly as they chose which database to diff.

The judge starts from a compact summary of the databases and their tables, then explores on demand: list/inspect tables, page rows, run a literal case-insensitive substring search over a table's complete contents, or run a single read-only SQL statement for joins, filters and aggregates.

Use this when the criterion names an artifact the agent produced ("the email sent to X", "the post to the Y channel") and asks something about its content — which is what database criteria almost always ask. Use the diff judge instead when the criterion genuinely needs open-ended change discovery ("nothing else was modified").
definitions.limitations: Judges the final database state only. It never sees a before-state, so it cannot prove the agent caused what it finds — a criterion that is already true on the pristine seed will pass vacuously. Author criteria that are false on the seed, or use the DB Diff judge when the criterion genuinely needs change discovery.

definitions.verifier_doc:
# DeepResearch Bench II Rubric

Scores one atomic, binary rubric item from DeepResearch Bench II (arXiv:2601.08536) against the agent's long-form research report.

## Overview

DeepResearch Bench II grades a deep-research agent by decomposing an expert-written investigative article into many small, independently checkable rubrics — 9,415 across the benchmark's 132 tasks, a median of 66 per task. Each rubric becomes one verifier, so a task's score is the share of its rubrics the report satisfies.

Judging is **batched**: the `deepresearch_bench_judge` helper runs once per task, sends rubrics to the judge 50 at a time along with the report, and caches every verdict. This verifier is a thin reader that pulls out its own result. A 200-rubric task therefore costs four judge calls rather than 200 — without batching the full report would be re-sent once per rubric.

## Supported Inputs

The agent's final assistant message, treated as the research report. The helper walks back to the last **non-empty assistant** message, so a trailing tool result does not get graded by mistake. Reports are truncated to 150,000 characters (matching the upstream `MAX_PAPER_CHARS`).

## Configuration

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rubric` | yes | The atomic requirement the report must satisfy. Should name a concrete fact, figure, or inference — not a vague topic. |
| `dimension` | yes | One of `info_recall`, `analysis`, `presentation`. Carried per verifier so per-dimension rates survive the fact that the server reassigns `verifier_index` on create. |
| `is_primary_objective` | no | Whether the rubric counts toward the task's primary score. Defaults to true. |

The blocked source list is read at grade time from the task's `drb2_blocked_urls` custom field (a JSON array of URLs), not from verifier config — it is per task, not per rubric.

## Examples

### Information recall

```
rubric:    Explicitly states that 2021 national land transfer income reached 5.6 trillion RMB.
dimension: info_recall
```
Satisfied only if that specific figure appears in the report.

### Presentation

```
rubric:    The report is divided into the two required sections named in the task.
dimension: presentation
```

## Edge Cases & Gotchas

- **The judge must echo each rubric's exact text back, and every batch is validated against that.** This is the load-bearing anti-degeneration device, copied from upstream (`"CRITICAL: the rubric_item text MUST match the input text EXACTLY"`). An earlier version of this eval keyed verdicts by index (`rubric_1`, `rubric_2`, …) with no validation, and a judge pattern-filled `{"score": 1}` for all 137 rubrics of a task without reading them — 41 of the 52 rubrics naming a specific paper cited a paper absent from the report, all marked satisfied. Re-typing each rubric forces per-item attention; the validator (count + exact-text match, retried up to `MAX_JSON_RETRIES`) catches a judge that didn't comply. **Do not "simplify" the response schema to indices or drop the validation** — the failure mode is silent and produces a plausible number rather than an error.
- **Blocked references are the anti-gaming mechanism.** Each task's rubrics were derived from a specific expert article. If the report satisfies a rubric but its evidence is drawn from that blocked article, the judge returns `-1` and the rubric scores **0.0** — an agent that simply locates and restates the source must not be rewarded. Populate `drb2_blocked_urls` or this protection is silently inert.
- `-1` and `0` both score 0.0. They are distinguished only by the `blocked` output field, which is what makes the benchmark's `blocked_rate` recoverable.
- If the agent produces no report at all, every rubric scores 0.0 and no judge call is made.
- A chunk the judge never answers validly **raises**, failing the grading run. It is deliberately not scored 0 — a silent 0 would understate the model instead of surfacing a grading failure. An individual out-of-range score (not 1/0/-1) does degrade to 0.0.
- Tasks exist in both Chinese and English; rubrics are written in the task's language and the judge is expected to grade in-language.

## Scoring

1.0 when the judge returns `1` (satisfied, with evidence, from an unblocked source). 0.0 for `0` (not satisfied) and for `-1` (satisfied via a blocked source). No partial credit — rubrics are binary by construction.

Pair with the `criteria_level_clamped_average` scoring method to reproduce the benchmark's published metric, which is `count(1) / total` per dimension.

## Output

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `satisfied` | Report meets the rubric with unblocked evidence. |
| `blocked` | Rubric met, but evidence came from a blocked source (upstream `-1`). |
| `reason` | Judge's justification. |
| `evidence` | Sentence(s) quoted from the report supporting the verdict. |
| `dimension` | Dimension the rubric was graded under. |

definitions.verifier_doc: Scores one physician-written rubric item from HealthBench Professional (arXiv:2604.27470) against the model's next turn in a real clinician conversation, using OpenAI's verbatim grader prompt. The whole conversation is shown to the judge, not just the final answer — 115 of the benchmark's 525 examples are multi-turn, and a criterion such as 'asks about current medications' is unjudgeable without the preceding turns. Criteria carry signed points (-10..+10); a negative criterion names an undesirable behaviour, so criteria_met = True applies a penalty. Pair with the healthbench_points_score scoring method, which reproduces the benchmark's formula exactly: sum of met points over the sum of POSITIVE points, unclamped (upstream clips the mean across examples, not each example, so a penalized response scores below zero on purpose). NOTE the resulting score is the benchmark's RAW example score. The paper's headline metric applies a further per-example length adjustment, s - 2.94e-5 * (chars - 2000), which cannot be computed in-platform because a scoring method never sees the trajectory; apply it offline, with the clip of the mean, before comparing to published numbers. Source: https://github.com/openai/simple-evals/blob/main/healthbench_eval.py

verifier_config_fields.description: How per-criterion scores roll up to the final score. 'scope_balanced' (default) = (deck_avg + slide_avg) / 2. 'unit_balanced' = mean over [deck_avg, slide_1_avg, ..., slide_N_avg]. 'criterion_balanced' = flat mean across every non-nan criterion score.

verifier_config_fields.label: Return nan when no scores
verifier_config_fields.description: If true, return nan as the final score when every criterion returned nan (nothing was actually scored). If false, return 0.0.

verifier_config_fields.label: Style Criteria
verifier_config_fields.description: List of style criteria to evaluate on the PPTX deck.

subschema.label: Criteria Name
subschema.description: Unique identifier for this criterion (e.g., 'font_consistency')

subschema.label: Criteria Prompt
subschema.description: LLM judge prompt describing what to evaluate for this criterion

subschema.label: Judge Mode
subschema.description: Whether to judge using extracted text metadata or rendered slide images

subschema.label: Criteria Scope
subschema.description: Whether this criterion applies to the whole deck or per-slide

subschema.label: Criteria Tag
subschema.description: Category tag for this criterion. Used to compute per-tag aggregate scores in the output.

verifier_config_fields.label: Agent Result Path
verifier_config_fields.description: Path to the PPTX file in the snapshot (auto-detected if not set)

verifier_output_fields.label: Detailed Results
verifier_output_fields.description: Nested per-criterion results with scores and rationales

verifier_output_fields.label: Deck Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Average score across deck-scoped criteria (nan if none scored)

verifier_output_fields.label: Slide Average
verifier_output_fields.description: Average of per-slide scores (nan if no slides scored)

verifier_output_fields.label: Final Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Aggregated final score per the configured aggregation_strategy

verifier_output_fields.label: Tag Scores
verifier_output_fields.description: Per-tag average scores keyed by criteria_tag (e.g., {'style': 0.85, 'output_correctness': 0.92})

verifier_output_fields.label: Aggregation Strategy Used
verifier_output_fields.description: Which aggregation strategy produced the final score

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Count
verifier_output_fields.description: Total number of criteria evaluated

verifier_output_fields.label: Slide Count
verifier_output_fields.description: Number of slides in the deck

definitions.verifier_doc: Multi-criteria style verifier for PPTX decks. Each criterion is scored {0, 1, nan} by an LLM judge using either extracted font/layout metadata (text mode) or rendered slide images (image mode). Criteria are scoped to either the whole deck or a single slide. Final score is computed by the configured aggregation strategy, and per-tag aggregate scores are emitted as a breakdown.

verifier_config_fields.label: Style Criteria
verifier_config_fields.description: List of style criteria to evaluate on the DOCX document.

subschema.label: Criteria Name
subschema.description: Unique identifier for this criterion (e.g., 'section_hierarchy').

subschema.label: Criteria Prompt
subschema.description: LLM judge prompt describing what to evaluate for this criterion.

subschema.label: Judge Mode
subschema.description: Whether to judge using extracted text metadata or rendered page images (which show tracked changes inline).

subschema.label: Criteria Scope
subschema.description: Whether this criterion applies to the whole document or per-page (most useful in image mode).

subschema.label: Criteria Tag
subschema.description: Category tag for this criterion.

subschema.label: Judge System Prompt
subschema.description: Optional system prompt prefix for additional judge context.

subschema.label: Requires Template
subschema.description: If true, this criterion is skipped (returns nan) unless a template_artifacts entry was configured and loaded.

subschema.label: Signed Weight
subschema.description: Optional signed rubric weight. The DOCX judge ignores it; it rides along so a weighted scoring method (redline_weighted_score) can reward a met positive criterion by +weight and penalise a met negative one by |weight|. Leave unset for unweighted scoring.

verifier_config_fields.label: Template Documents
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional: select template DOCX(s) the output should be redlining against. Loaded into the judge context for criteria that compare the output to a template (e.g., section hierarchy matches template).

verifier_config_fields.label: Agent Result Path
verifier_config_fields.description: Path to the output DOCX in the final snapshot (auto-detected if not set).

verifier_config_fields.label: Expected Redline Author
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional validity gate. When set, the output must be a loadable DOCX carrying at least one tracked change or comment attributed to this author, else the verifier returns 0 without an LLM call (gate_failed). Matched case-insensitively as a substring of an author found in the DOCX. Leave unset to disable the gate (backwards-compatible default).

verifier_output_fields.label: Detailed Results
verifier_output_fields.description: Nested per-criterion results with scores and rationales.

verifier_output_fields.label: Validity Gate Failed
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the expected-redline-author gate rejected the output before grading. Present only when the gate was configured and failed; the result then has no detailed_results and scores 0.

verifier_output_fields.label: Validity Gate Reason
verifier_output_fields.description: Why the validity gate failed (authors present vs expected).

verifier_output_fields.label: Invalid Output
verifier_output_fields.description: True when the model produced no gradeable output (a benchmark outcome scored 0), e.g. a missing output DOCX or a failed validity gate. The typed signal a scorer/reducer consumes instead of parsing an error string.

verifier_output_fields.label: Invalid Output Reason
verifier_output_fields.description: Why the output was invalid when invalid_output is true, e.g. 'missing_docx' or 'gate_failed'.

verifier_output_fields.label: Document Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Average score across document-scoped criteria.

verifier_output_fields.label: Page Average
verifier_output_fields.description: Average of per-page scores.

verifier_output_fields.label: Final Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Aggregated final score.

verifier_output_fields.label: Criteria Count
verifier_output_fields.description: Total number of criteria evaluated.

verifier_output_fields.label: Page Count
verifier_output_fields.description: Number of pages in the rendered document.

verifier_output_fields.label: Template Used
verifier_output_fields.description: Name of the template artifact (if any) used as context.

definitions.verifier_doc: Batched LLM grading of Word documents on style criteria. Supports two scopes (document-level or per-page) and two judge modes: text (using extracted paragraph metadata + redlines summary) or image (using rendered PNGs showing tracked changes). Optional template documents auto-fail criteria if no template loads.

verifier_config_fields.label: Template Document
verifier_config_fields.description: Select the template DOCX (typically a world file) that the model output is expected to redline. The verifier passes only if all edits in the output are inside tracked changes or comments.

verifier_config_fields.label: Agent Result Path
verifier_config_fields.description: Path to the output DOCX in the final snapshot (auto-detected if not set).

verifier_output_fields.label: Rationale
verifier_output_fields.description: Explanation of pass/fail; on fail, includes a text diff between the accepted-output and the template.

verifier_output_fields.label: Output Path
verifier_output_fields.description: Path of the docx that was evaluated.

verifier_output_fields.label: Template Name
verifier_output_fields.description: Name of the template artifact used for comparison.

definitions.verifier_doc: Verifies that every NEW edit in an output DOCX is tracked (in w:ins/w:del/w:moveFrom/w:moveTo elements or comments). Normalizes and compares all editorial parts (document.xml, footnotes.xml, endnotes.xml, headers/footers) after stripping pre-existing tracked changes from the template, enabling corporate-law workflows where templates carry prior negotiation history.

verifier_config_fields.label: Template Workbook
verifier_config_fields.description: Select the template xlsx (typically a world file) the model started from. Used only as a structural reference for the agent.

verifier_config_fields.label: Output Workbook Path
verifier_config_fields.description: Path to the model's output xlsx in the final snapshot. Leave blank to auto-detect the first .xlsx.

verifier_config_fields.label: Sensitivity Analyses
verifier_config_fields.description: One entry per sensitivity analysis. For each, the agent applies the prompt's input change to the output workbook, and the verifier scores three sub-criteria against the expected output cells.

subschema.label: SA Name
subschema.description: Short identifier, e.g. 'wacc_up_2pp'. Used in the result rationale.

subschema.label: SA Prompt
subschema.description: Natural-language description of the input change, handed to the agent. Example: 'Change the WACC from 9% to 11%.'

subschema.label: Expected Outputs (JSON)
subschema.description: JSON array of expected output cell movements. Each item: {"label": "Enterprise Value", "sheet": "DCF", "cell": "E27", "from": 1200, "to": 980, "tolerance_pct": 0.02}. `from` is optional (used in rationale); `to` and cell coordinates are required; `tolerance_pct` defaults to 0.02.

verifier_config_fields.label: Sub-criterion Weights (JSON)
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional JSON overriding the per-sub-criterion weights. Default: {"anything_changed": 0.2, "at_least_one_output_changed": 0.3, "all_outputs_correct": 0.5}. Weights are normalized.

verifier_config_fields.label: Max Agent Iterations
verifier_config_fields.description: Per-SA cap on agent tool-use iterations. Default: 12.

verifier_config_fields.label: Agent Model Override
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional model id (litellm format). Defaults to the grading_settings.llm_judge_model.

verifier_output_fields.label: Final Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Mean of per-SA weighted scores.

verifier_output_fields.label: Summary
verifier_output_fields.description: Per-SA sub-criterion scores in 'name: a/b/c (w=…)' form, joined by ' | '.

verifier_output_fields.label: Output Path
verifier_output_fields.description: Path of the output xlsx that was evaluated.

verifier_output_fields.label: Per-SA Results
verifier_output_fields.description: Detailed per-SA results: agent success flag, three sub-criterion scores with rationales, the recalculated workbook as a data: URL, the agent tool-call log, and the SA's weighted score.

verifier_output_fields.label: Weights Used
verifier_output_fields.description: Effective weights after parsing weights_json.

definitions.verifier_doc: Grades investment-banking work products (Excel sensitivity analyses) by having an LLM agent re-calculate the workbook and comparing outputs. Evaluates three binary sub-criteria (anything_changed, at_least_one_output_changed, all_outputs_correct) weighted by sensitivity analysis, returning weighted average score.

verifier_config_fields.label: Expected Prefix
verifier_config_fields.description: The alphanumeric hash string the model must prepend to its response.

verifier_config_fields.label: Expected Answer
verifier_config_fields.description: The full expected answer (including the prefix).

verifier_output_fields.label: Has Correct Prefix
verifier_output_fields.description: Whether the response starts with the expected hash prefix.

verifier_output_fields.label: Similarity Score
verifier_output_fields.description: SequenceMatcher ratio between stripped response and expected answer (0.0-1.0).

verifier_output_fields.label: Rationale
verifier_output_fields.description: Explanation of the grading result.

definitions.verifier_doc: MRCR (Multi-Round Co-reference Resolution) verifier. Checks that the response starts with the expected hash prefix, then computes difflib.SequenceMatcher similarity ratio between the stripped response and expected answer.

eval_config_fields.label: Judge prompt
eval_config_fields.description: How the judge reviews each criterion. Pick the style that matches what your rubric is about — reviewing code changes, evaluating a plan, checking the agent's behavior, or grading an answer.

eval_config_fields.label: What's being graded
eval_config_fields.description: What the agent produced that is being graded (code output, trajectory, final answer, etc). Multiple sources are concatenated under their section headers.

eval_config_fields.label: Task context sources
eval_config_fields.description: Additional context given to the judge (e.g. the original prompt). These are files that the judge model will see as additional context in the prompt.

eval_config_fields.label: Weight factors (optional override)

verifier_config_fields.description: What the judge should evaluate the agent against.

verifier_config_fields.label: Rationale

verifier_config_fields.label: Weight
verifier_config_fields.description: How important this criterion is. The world's weight scheme maps this label to a numeric weight contribution.

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge grade

eval_config_fields.label: What's being graded

verifier_config_fields.label: GDPval Task ID
verifier_config_fields.description: UUID from the openai/gdpval HuggingFace dataset

verifier_config_fields.label: GDPval Judge Mode
verifier_config_fields.description: pairwise compares the model deliverable against the human gold deliverable. rubric_item grades one rubric criterion. Blank is treated as legacy dual mode.

verifier_config_fields.label: Gold Deliverable URLs

verifier_config_fields.label: Rubric JSON
verifier_config_fields.description: One structured human-authored rubric item for split rubric_item verifiers, encoded as a one-element JSON list. Legacy dual-mode verifiers may contain the full rubric_json column from the GDPval dataset.

verifier_config_fields.label: Criterion
verifier_config_fields.description: Human-readable rubric criterion text for rubric display.

verifier_config_fields.label: Rubric Item ID
verifier_config_fields.description: Human-authored rubric item UUID from the GDPval dataset.

verifier_config_fields.label: Rubric Item Score
verifier_config_fields.description: Point weight for this GDPval rubric item.

verifier_config_fields.label: Judge Model Override
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional override for the judge model. If empty, the grading run's default judge is used.

verifier_config_fields.label: GDPval Sector
verifier_config_fields.description: GDPval sector label (analytics only).

verifier_config_fields.label: GDPval Occupation
verifier_config_fields.description: GDPval occupation label (analytics only).

verifier_output_fields.description: {0.0, 0.5, 1.0} — model loses / ties / wins vs the human gold deliverable

verifier_output_fields.label: Pairwise Verdict
verifier_output_fields.description: Judge verdict letter (A/B/TIE), post-unswap

verifier_output_fields.label: Pairwise Rationale
verifier_output_fields.description: Judge's rationale for the pairwise verdict

verifier_output_fields.label: A/B Swap
verifier_output_fields.description: True if model deliverable was shown as B (gold as A)

verifier_output_fields.label: Rubric Score
verifier_output_fields.description: Normalized rubric score in [0, 1] = awarded weight / total weight

verifier_output_fields.label: Rubric Awarded Weight
verifier_output_fields.description: Sum of point values awarded across rubric items

verifier_output_fields.label: Rubric Total Weight
verifier_output_fields.description: Sum of absolute point values across all rubric items

verifier_output_fields.label: Rubric Breakdown
verifier_output_fields.description: Per-rubric-item pass/fail with judge rationale

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge Model Used
verifier_output_fields.description: Model that produced the verdicts (override or grading default)

verifier_output_fields.label: Gold Files
verifier_output_fields.description: Filenames of the human-reference deliverables compared against

verifier_output_fields.label: Model Files
verifier_output_fields.description: Filenames produced by the agent in the final snapshot

definitions.verifier_doc: GDPval judge: split pairwise verifiers compare model deliverables against human gold deliverables, and split rubric_item verifiers grade one human-authored criterion each. Legacy blank-mode verifiers still run dual mode for staged data repair. gdpval_score selects the headline metric. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04374

Sparta Mirror: returns the sparta_external_agent's Taiga `final_score` as the verifier score. No knobs and no helpers — the agent already fetched the grade and wrote it to trajectory_output. Hard-fails when final_score is missing or non-numeric (wrong agent / non-terminal Taiga run).

Sparta Agentic Grading: opens an SSE stream to Taiga's grading transcript endpoint for the trajectory's problem_run_id, emits one grading_transcript_event log per delta (same shape sparta_external_agent emits to trajectory_logs), and returns the agent-resolved final_score as the verifier score. Score matches sparta_mirror; novel piece is the per-delta grading transcript replay surfaced via grading_logs.

verifier_output_fields.label: Normalized Score
verifier_output_fields.description: The MCP reward's normalized_score (0-1).

verifier_output_fields.label: Subscores
verifier_output_fields.description: Per-criterion MCP subscores (name/score/max_score/weight).

verifier_output_fields.label: Model Answer
verifier_output_fields.description: The agent's answer the MCP grader scored.

verifier_output_fields.label: Golden Answer
verifier_output_fields.description: The reference answer the MCP grader compared against.

verifier_output_fields.label: Is Correct
verifier_output_fields.description: Whether the MCP grader judged the answer correct.

verifier_output_fields.label: Grader Reasoning
verifier_output_fields.description: The MCP grader's reasoning for the grade.

verifier_output_fields.label: Other Metadata
verifier_output_fields.description: Any MCP reward metadata keys beyond the promoted set — lossless catch-all for non-default graders.

definitions.verifier_doc: Sparta MCP Grading: sibling of sparta_agentic_grading for Taiga envs that grade with a `mcp` strategy (the default code-based grade_problem grader). Returns the agent-resolved final_score as the verifier score (same as sparta_mirror / sparta_agentic_grading) and captures the MCP reward's metadata (model_answer, golden_answer, is_correct, grader_reasoning) plus per-criterion subscores into verifier_result_values. Taiga lazy-loads reward metadata, so the verifier fetches it via a single GET /jobs/{job_id}/problems?include_grading_metadata=true; a fetch miss (no job id, transport/HTTP failure, problem-run or reward not found) fails the verifier — there is no MCP grade to surface without it. No grading_logs replay.

verifier_config_fields.label: Criteria
verifier_config_fields.description: What should be verified about the VCA behavior?

verifier_config_fields.label: Criteria Explanation
verifier_config_fields.description: Additional context for the criteria

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge Grade
verifier_output_fields.description: Pass or fail grade from LLM

verifier_output_fields.label: Rationale
verifier_output_fields.description: Explanation for the grade

verifier_output_fields.label: VCA ID
verifier_output_fields.description: Virtual coworker actor id

verifier_output_fields.label: TA Trajectory ID
verifier_output_fields.description: Parent target-agent trajectory id

definitions.verifier_doc: LLM judge for Virtual Coworker Agent (VCA) behavior grading. Evaluates a single VCA's behavior against a criterion using its trajectory, coordinator evidence, and events. Only runs on virtual_coworker_agent evaluation targets; requires vca_id metadata.

verifier_config_fields.label: File Pattern
verifier_config_fields.description: Glob pattern to locate CSV/Excel file (e.g., '*.csv', 'output.xlsx')

verifier_config_fields.label: Sheet Name
verifier_config_fields.description: Sheet name for Excel files (optional, defaults to first sheet). Takes precedence over Sheet Number.

verifier_config_fields.label: Sheet Number
verifier_config_fields.description: 0-based sheet index for Excel files (optional). Ignored if Sheet Name is set.

verifier_config_fields.label: Allow Row Reorder
verifier_config_fields.description: If true, rows can appear in any order (matched by content or key columns)

verifier_config_fields.label: Allow Column Reorder
verifier_config_fields.description: If true, columns can appear in any order (matched by header name)

verifier_config_fields.label: Allow Extra Columns
verifier_config_fields.description: If true, agent output may have additional columns beyond those in the golden file

verifier_config_fields.label: Numeric Tolerance
verifier_config_fields.description: Relative tolerance for numeric comparisons (default: 0.0001 = 0.01%)

verifier_config_fields.label: Case Sensitive
verifier_config_fields.description: Whether string comparisons are case-sensitive

verifier_config_fields.label: Key Columns
verifier_config_fields.description: Comma-separated column names for row matching when Allow Row Reorder is enabled. If empty, all columns are used for matching.

verifier_output_fields.label: Matched Rows
verifier_output_fields.description: Number of golden rows that matched in the agent output

verifier_output_fields.label: Total Golden Rows
verifier_output_fields.description: Total data rows in the golden file (excluding header)

verifier_output_fields.label: File Found
verifier_output_fields.description: Path of the file matched in the agent snapshot

verifier_output_fields.label: Mismatched Rows
verifier_output_fields.description: Details of the first rows that did not match

definitions.verifier_doc: Compares CSV/Excel tabular data in agent output against golden snapshot files. Supports configurable row/column reordering, numeric tolerance, and case sensitivity. Score = matched golden rows / total golden rows. Multiple golden snapshots: passes if ANY matches fully.

verifier_config_fields.label: Verification Prompt
verifier_config_fields.description: What the LLM should verify about the running app (e.g. 'sign in and confirm a new todo persists after reload').

verifier_config_fields.label: Launch Script
verifier_config_fields.description: Shell script (bash) that STARTS your app and makes it listen on $BUA_APP_PORT — use the variable, don't hardcode a port. cwd is your app source. The default grading sandbox has python3 only (no node/redis/apt); turn on 'Run in Env Image' for apps that need a build step, a backend, or system deps. Login creds (if set) arrive as $BUA_LOGIN_URL / _USERNAME / _PASSWORD.

verifier_config_fields.label: Login
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional credentials passed to the app env and the LLM. Shape: {"url": "...", "username": "...", "password": "...", "extra": {"key": "value"}}.

verifier_config_fields.label: App Port
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional fixed port. If omitted, a free port is auto-allocated per run (recommended — avoids collisions) and exposed as $BUA_APP_PORT.

verifier_config_fields.label: Startup Timeout (s)
verifier_config_fields.description: How long to wait for the app port to become reachable before failing.

verifier_config_fields.label: Max Iterations
verifier_config_fields.description: Maximum browser tool-loop iterations before the verifier gives up.

verifier_config_fields.label: Run in Env Image
verifier_config_fields.description: Launch the app inside the task's real platform image (node/redis/deps + the platform's own services) instead of the bare grading sandbox. Turn this on for apps that need a build step, a backend, or system deps. The image is resolved from the task's platform.

verifier_config_fields.label: App Dir (Env Image)
verifier_config_fields.description: Working dir the launch/restore scripts run in — defaults to where the captured filesystem restores (/filesystem). Override if the app lives elsewhere in the image. The captured .apps_data is at $BUA_APPS_DATA_DIR.

verifier_config_fields.label: Restore Script (Env Image)
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional shell run before the launch script to restore app state. The captured .apps_data/ is available at $BUA_APPS_DATA_DIR (e.g. `psql < "$BUA_APPS_DATA_DIR"/dump.sql`).

verifier_config_fields.label: Provision Timeout (s, Env Image)
verifier_config_fields.description: Readiness budget for the env-image path (image pull + boot + app start), separate from Startup Timeout.

verifier_config_fields.label: Test Plan
verifier_config_fields.description: Optional per-step point weights: [{"name": "...", "points": N}, ...]. When set, the judge awards points per step and the score is fractional (points earned / full points) instead of binary. Absent → binary pass/fail. The step prose the judge reads still lives in Verification Prompt.

verifier_output_fields.label: Judge Grade
verifier_output_fields.description: Pass or fail verdict from the browser-driving LLM (pass iff a perfect grade when a test plan is set).

verifier_output_fields.label: Rationale
verifier_output_fields.description: Explanation for the verdict (credentials redacted).

verifier_output_fields.label: Action Log
verifier_output_fields.description: Sequence of browser tools the LLM invoked (credentials redacted).

verifier_output_fields.label: Points Earned
verifier_output_fields.description: Points the judge awarded across the test plan (fractional path only).

verifier_output_fields.label: Full Points
verifier_output_fields.description: Authored maximum points for the test plan (fractional path only).

verifier_output_fields.label: Step Breakdown
verifier_output_fields.description: Per-step points the judge awarded (fractional path only).

definitions.verifier_doc: Grades a one-shotted browser-use web application by launching it in the grading sandbox (via a config-provided launch script) and letting an LLM drive a live headless browser against it to verify behavior. Tool-augmented, like db_diff_llm_tools, but the target is a running app instead of a DB diff. Not annotator-friendly: launch script + login are admin/code-data authored.

verifier_output_fields.label: Supported
verifier_output_fields.description: pass/fail — whether the app exposes the tools the workflow needs.

verifier_output_fields.label: Tools OK
verifier_output_fields.description: pass/fail — whether every tool the agent called worked as expected.

verifier_output_fields.label: Seed OK

definitions.verifier_doc:
The single locked verifier for **Automated Workflow Testing for Apps** (RLS-8320).

A workflow test is a free-text description of a real task a user would do, run by a fixed agent harness on the app's **default seed data**. This verifier runs one LLM judge over the resulting trajectory and reads three facets from the end-state:

- **Supported** — does the app expose the tools the workflow needs? (`false` when a required capability has no tool at all)
- **Tools OK** — did the tools the agent called work as expected? (`false` when an existing tool errored or misbehaved)
- **Seed OK** — was the default seed data sufficient to complete the workflow? (`false` when required data was missing)

Overall pass requires all three. The judge also records `tools_covered` (the tools the trajectory exercised) to feed the App-Hub Tools-coverage rollup.

Unlike the general-purpose output LLM judge, this verifier has **no user-editable config**: the only authored input is the workflow prompt (carried on the task), and both the harness and the judge model are pinned server-side. Because the agent and judge are non-deterministic, results are **report-only** — an admin can flag a run Inconclusive.
definitions.limitations: Locked, non-deterministic LLM judge for app workflow tests — report-only, not a deploy gate, and not annotator-configurable (prompt-only; the harness and judge model are pinned server-side).

definitions.verifier_doc:
Video verifier for deliverables the LLM/VLM judges can't grade. Streams the target video out of the final snapshot to disk in bounded chunks (so multi-gigabyte deliverables never load into memory), then runs two kinds of checks: deterministic ffprobe/ffmpeg checks (resolution, frame rate, codec, duration, audio true-peak/integrated loudness, per-window loudness) and content checks that sample frames (vlm_frames) or extract the audio (audio_content) and ask the grading judge model whether a criterion holds. Score is 1.0 when the checks pass (per 'mode'; 'fraction' gives partial credit).

Scope notes: 'audio_true_peak' and 'audio_integrated_loudness' measure the WHOLE file across every element in the mix, so they cannot verify a criterion scoped to one element (e.g. 'dialogue normalized to -4 dBFS') — use 'audio_window' over the relevant span for that. Set File Name whenever the snapshot also contains source footage: a File Pattern that matches more than one video is rejected rather than guessed at.
